title: Optimized DPPH Assay for Measuring Antioxidant Activity of Proteins
author: Nicklisch, Waite

steps.title: Prepare 2 mM DPPH stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve DPPH in methanol to make a 2 mM solution, prepare it fresh, wrap the container in aluminum foil to avoid photochemical decomposition, and keep it protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare citrate‑phosphate buffers
steps.instruction: Make 0.1 M citrate‑phosphate buffer solutions adjusted to final pH 3, pH 5, and pH 7.5 as described in the referenced method.

steps.title: Add Triton X‑100 to buffer
steps.instruction: To each 9.7 mL of the 0.1 M citrate‑phosphate buffer add 300 µL of a 10 % (v/v) Triton X‑100 solution, yielding a final detergent concentration of 0.3 % (v/v) Triton X‑100. No pH shift occurs upon addition.

steps.title: Prepare assay samples
steps.instruction: For antioxidant tests, directly reconstitute the control antioxidant compound to final concentrations of 2.5, 5, 10, 15, and 20 µM in 950 µL of the detergent‑based assay buffer. For protein tests, freeze‑dry 5 µmol of the pure protein, dissolve it in the same assay buffer (0.1 M citrate‑phosphate + 0.3 % Triton X‑100) to a final volume of 950 µL. For buffer‑only controls, use 950 µL of the detergent‑based buffer alone.

steps.title: Start DPPH reaction
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the freshly prepared 2 mM methanolic DPPH stock to each 950 µL sample (protein, antioxidant, or buffer) to obtain a final DPPH concentration of 100 µM. For the pH‑dependence experiment, add 50 µL of DPPH solutions at 0.5, 1, 2, 3, or 4 mM to achieve final DPPH concentrations of 25, 50, 100, 150, or 200 µM respectively.

steps.title: Mix reaction gently
steps.instruction: Pipette half the reaction volume (500 µL) up and down 3–5 times to mix. Use a fresh pipette tip for each triplicate sample to avoid carry‑over, especially at higher antioxidant/DPPH ratios.

steps.title: Seal cuvettes and incubate
steps.instruction: Seal each cuvette with Parafilm, keep the cuvettes wrapped in aluminum foil, and incubate at room temperature (RT). For the standard assay, record absorbance after 5 min, 60 min, and 16 h. For the pH‑dependence assay, record after 15 min (single‑time point) or after 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, and 60 min for the 100 µM DPPH condition. For antioxidant and protein assays, record after 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105, and 120 min (protein assay also includes a 2‑min measurement right after mixing).

steps.title: Centrifuge before measurement
steps.instruction: Immediately prior to each absorbance reading, centrifuge the cuvette for 1 min at 17 000 × g. If a precipitate is visible, transfer the clear supernatant to a fresh cuvette for measurement; precipitation can increase turbidity and cause false‑negative results.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 515 nm
steps.instruction: Using a spectrophotometer, measure the absorbance at 515 nm in triplicate for each time point. For the initial buffer‑only experiment, perform measurements in double‑distilled water, pure methanol, and water containing varying concentrations of the mild non‑ionic detergents Tween 20 or Triton X‑100 as illustrated in Fig. 1. Keep all samples in the dark at RT during measurements. For the protein assay, begin the spectrophotometric reading within 1–2 min of reaction start.
